Local to the places I ride, the maps are generally complete and accurate.

Sometimes it doesnΓÇÖt matter how good your GPS receiver is, and the signal connection will still be lost.  If your phone is constantly losing GPS connection, either your phoneΓÇÖs receiver is low quality, the weather is impeding the connection, or youΓÇÖre simply in a location where a GPS receiver is going to constantly drop connection no matter how good your receiver is.  I hope this helps.

title: My go to app for finding and following all types of trails

As a result, it is an ever growing guide to the outdoors that should be the first stop for anyone who enjoys outdoor activities.

There are a couple of limitations I should point out. First, in areas with poor cell phone coverage, the app can lead you off course by 5-10 meters, just enough to make you start getting worried. Second, its coverage of paddling routes is still thin. (Come on you kayakers, do your part!). Finally, although I cannot give accurate numbers, the app is way short on showing camp sites. This is a
Problem if you want to plan a backpacking trip involving 2 or more overnight stays. Other apps appear to give better coverage of campsites, but I do not believe they are as carefully curated as AllTrails, so they can lead you to nonexistent campsites or, worse yet, private property.

Bottom line, this should be the starting point for anyone who wants to enjoy the great outdoors. Nevertheless, NO app should replace the common sense measures of having a backup map, appropriate safety gear, and, for longer trips, letting someone know your plans.

review: I love this app but they made it worse when they recently changed the system for filtering by star rating. review: The first time I used Alltrails, it was the free version. title: Great app, one big problem in pro version
review:
This is a fantastic app and really useful for hiking. It would be a wholehearted recommendation if it wasn't for one problem I keep running into.

The main reason for buying the pro version is offline maps access. Most trails I do are not where data coverage is available. So offline maps are critical.

Hiwever, once downloaded, they just go away (expire?) within a day or so. This is incredibly frustrating given how much effort I took to slowly download these maps in poor data areas,only to find it magically disappeared before the hike.

Also the process of selecting a custom nap for offline download requires substantial data which makes it almost impossible to select in low bw areas. This is likely not an app problem, but if the selection UI can somehow use very low detail data to just select region, that would be great.

Mostly just please fix offline map expiry problem!
